lines.text: In 2022, about half of FSA holders forfeited their own money.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-two, about half of FSA holders forfeited their own money.

lines.text: The average forfeit was $441, per an EBRI study of 3.2 million accounts.
lines.say: The average forfeit was four hundred forty-one dollars, according to an EBRI study of three point two million accounts.

lines.text: That was up from $339 in 2019.
lines.say: That was up from three hundred thirty-nine dollars in twenty nineteen.

lines.text: That money wasn't stolen. It just hit a deadline nobody was watching.
lines.say: That money wasn't stolen. It just hit a deadline nobody was watching.

lines.text: Year-end money runs on two dates: December 31, 2026, and April 15, 2027.
lines.say: Year-end money runs on two dates: December thirty-first, twenty twenty-six, and April fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: So here's the full checklist: taxes, benefits, accounts and goals, with the official 2026 numbers.
lines.say: So here's the full checklist: taxes, benefits, accounts and goals, with the official twenty twenty-six numbers.

lines.text: Education, not advice. Every limit here is for tax year 2026 and comes from the IRS.
lines.say: Education, not advice. Every limit here is for tax year twenty twenty-six and comes from the IRS.

lines.text: Chapter 1: Two deadlines.
lines.say: Chapter one: two deadlines.

lines.text: Most year-end moves have to happen by December 31: 401(k) paycheck contributions, FSA spending in many plans, and required withdrawals.
lines.say: Most year-end moves have to happen by December thirty-first: 401(k) paycheck contributions, FSA spending in many plans, and required withdrawals.

lines.text: Some FSA plans add a grace period. For a calendar-year plan, that can run to March 15, 2027.
lines.say: Some FSA plans add a grace period. For a calendar-year plan, that can run to March fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: And IRA and HSA contributions for 2026 can wait until the filing deadline, April 15, 2027.
lines.say: And IRA and HSA contributions for twenty twenty-six can wait until the filing deadline, April fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: Here's the catch. A 401(k) has no do-over. Money has to come out of a paycheck dated in 2026.
lines.say: Here's the catch. A 401(k) has no do-over. The money has to come out of a paycheck dated in twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: December's last paychecks are the final chance to change that, and payroll often needs lead time.
lines.say: December's last paychecks are the final chance to change that, and payroll often needs lead time.

lines.text: Chapter 2: Retirement and HSA limits.
lines.say: Chapter two: retirement and HSA limits.

lines.text: For 2026, the 401(k) and 403(b) limit is $24,500.
lines.say: For twenty twenty-six, the 401(k) and 403(b) limit is twenty-four thousand five hundred dollars.

lines.text: Here's the IRS limit since 2016. It was $18,000 then and has climbed in most years since.
lines.say: Here's the IRS limit since twenty sixteen. It was eighteen thousand dollars then, and it has climbed in most years since.

lines.text: The biggest one-year jump was 2023, up $2,000 to $22,500. For 2026 it rose $1,000.
lines.say: The biggest one-year jump was twenty twenty-three, up two thousand dollars to twenty-two thousand five hundred. For twenty twenty-six it rose one thousand dollars.

lines.text: Turning 50 or older by December 31 adds a catch-up of $8,000, for a total of $32,500.
lines.say: Turning fifty or older by December thirty-first adds a catch-up of eight thousand dollars, for a total of thirty-two thousand five hundred.

lines.text: Ages 60 through 63 get a bigger super catch-up of $11,250.
lines.say: Ages sixty through sixty-three get a bigger super catch-up of eleven thousand two hundred fifty dollars.

lines.text: Example: a 61-year-old can defer $24,500 plus $11,250. That's $35,750 for 2026.
lines.say: Example: a sixty-one-year-old can defer twenty-four thousand five hundred plus eleven thousand two hundred fifty. That's thirty-five thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: New in 2026: if your 2025 wages from that employer topped $150,000, catch-ups have to go in as Roth.
lines.say: New in twenty twenty-six: if your twenty twenty-five wages from that employer topped one hundred fifty thousand dollars, catch-ups have to go in as Roth.

lines.text: Roth means after-tax now. Plans without a Roth option may not offer those workers a catch-up at all.
lines.say: Roth means after-tax now. Plans without a Roth option may not offer those workers a catch-up at all.

lines.text: IRAs rose too. The 2026 limit is $7,500, plus $1,100 more at age 50 and up, for $8,600.
lines.say: IRAs rose too. The twenty twenty-six limit is seven thousand five hundred dollars, plus eleven hundred more at age fifty and up, for eight thousand six hundred.

lines.text: Roth IRAs were our November 11 guide. Here, the key date is April 15, 2027.
lines.say: Roth IRAs were our November eleventh guide. Here, the key date is April fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: HSAs, paired with high-deductible health plans, have a 2026 limit of $4,400 for self-only coverage.
lines.say: HSAs, paired with high-deductible health plans, have a twenty twenty-six limit of four thousand four hundred dollars for self-only coverage.

lines.text: Family coverage gets $8,750, and people 55 or older can add $1,000.
lines.say: Family coverage gets eight thousand seven hundred fifty dollars, and people fifty-five or older can add one thousand dollars.

lines.text: Unlike an FSA, HSA money doesn't vanish on December 31. It stays in the account, year after year.
lines.say: Unlike an FSA, HSA money doesn't vanish on December thirty-first. It stays in the account, year after year.

lines.text: Chapter 3: Benefits you can lose.
lines.say: Chapter three: benefits you can lose.

lines.text: A health FSA lets workers set aside pre-tax pay for medical costs. The 2026 limit is $3,400.
lines.say: A health FSA lets workers set aside pre-tax pay for medical costs. The twenty twenty-six limit is three thousand four hundred dollars.

lines.text: Whatever isn't used by the plan's deadline can be forfeited. But plans can soften that in one of two ways, not both.
lines.say: Whatever isn't used by the plan's deadline can be forfeited. But plans can soften that in one of two ways, not both.

lines.text: Option one is a carryover. For 2026 plan years, up to $680 can roll into 2027.
lines.say: Option one is a carryover. For twenty twenty-six plan years, up to six hundred eighty dollars can roll into twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: Option two is a grace period of up to two and a half months. That's March 15, 2027 for a calendar-year plan.
lines.say: Option two is a grace period of up to two and a half months. That's March fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven, for a calendar-year plan.

lines.text: Or the plan offers neither. Then it's pure use it or lose it at year-end.
lines.say: Or the plan offers neither. Then it's pure use it or lose it at year-end.

lines.text: Example: someone put in $3,400 and has spent $2,500 by mid-December. That leaves $900.
lines.say: Example: someone put in three thousand four hundred dollars and has spent twenty-five hundred by mid-December. That leaves nine hundred dollars.

lines.text: With a carryover plan, $680 rolls forward and $220 is lost.
lines.say: With a carryover plan, six hundred eighty rolls forward, and two hundred twenty dollars is lost.

lines.text: With a grace period, all $900 can still be spent by March 15. With neither, all $900 is gone.
lines.say: With a grace period, all nine hundred can still be spent by March fifteenth. With neither, all nine hundred dollars is gone.

lines.text: That's why people check the plan's rules and balance in early December. Glasses, prescriptions and dental work are common last-minute uses.
lines.say: That's why people check the plan's rules and balance in early December. Glasses, prescriptions and dental work are common last-minute uses.

lines.text: The dependent care FSA got bigger. Under the 2025 tax law, its limit rose from $5,000 to $7,500 for 2026.
lines.say: The dependent care FSA got bigger. Under the twenty twenty-five tax law, its limit rose from five thousand dollars to seventy-five hundred for twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: That's for things like daycare and after-school care. Employers don't have to adopt the higher limit, so plans vary.
lines.say: That's for things like daycare and after-school care. Employers don't have to adopt the higher limit, so plans vary.

lines.text: And by December, open enrollment has closed at most employers, so 2027 benefit picks are usually locked in.
lines.say: And by December, open enrollment has closed at most employers, so twenty twenty-seven benefit picks are usually locked in.

lines.text: Picking a health plan was our November 4 guide. On a year-end checklist, it's one line: confirm the 2027 elections came through.
lines.say: Picking a health plan was our November fourth guide. On a year-end checklist, it's one line: confirm the twenty twenty-seven elections came through.

lines.text: Chapter 4: Investments, gifts and RMDs.
lines.say: Chapter four: investments, gifts and R M Ds.

lines.text: A tax rate that sounds made up: 0% on long-term gains.
lines.say: A tax rate that sounds made up: zero percent on long-term gains.

lines.text: For 2026, it applies to single filers with taxable income up to $49,450, and joint filers up to $98,900.
lines.say: For twenty twenty-six, it applies to single filers with taxable income up to forty-nine thousand four hundred fifty dollars, and joint filers up to ninety-eight thousand nine hundred.

lines.text: Long-term means held more than a year. Gains on assets held a year or less are taxed like regular income.
lines.say: Long-term means held more than a year. Gains on assets held a year or less are taxed like regular income.

lines.text: Example: a single filer earns $54,100 in wages. Subtract the $16,100 standard deduction, and taxable income is $38,000.
lines.say: Example: a single filer earns fifty-four thousand one hundred dollars in wages. Subtract the sixteen thousand one hundred dollar standard deduction, and taxable income is thirty-eight thousand.

lines.text: That leaves $11,450 of room for long-term gains at 0% federally.
lines.say: That leaves eleven thousand four hundred fifty dollars of room for long-term gains at zero percent federally.

lines.text: Some people sell winners in that range by December 31 to lock in gains at 0%. State taxes can still apply.
lines.say: Some people sell winners in that range by December thirty-first to lock in gains at zero percent. State taxes can still apply.

lines.text: The flip side is tax-loss harvesting: selling investments that are down to offset gains.
lines.say: The flip side is tax-loss harvesting: selling investments that are down to offset gains.

lines.text: Example: $2,000 of gains and $7,000 of losses in 2026. That nets to a $5,000 loss.
lines.say: Example: two thousand dollars of gains and seven thousand dollars of losses in twenty twenty-six. That nets to a five thousand dollar loss.

lines.text: Up to $3,000 of net loss can offset regular income each year. The other $2,000 carries forward to 2027.
lines.say: Up to three thousand dollars of net loss can offset regular income each year. The other two thousand carries forward to twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: But there's the wash-sale rule. Buy the same or a substantially identical investment within 30 days before or after, and the loss is disallowed.
lines.say: But there's the wash-sale rule. Buy the same or a substantially identical investment within thirty days before or after, and the loss is disallowed.

lines.text: That's a 61-day window. The loss isn't erased; it moves into the new shares' cost, and waits until those shares are sold.
lines.say: That's a sixty-one-day window. The loss isn't erased; it moves into the new shares' cost, and waits until those shares are sold.

lines.text: Harvesting losses only works in taxable accounts. And buying the same fund in an IRA inside the window can still trigger a wash sale.
lines.say: Harvesting losses only works in taxable accounts. And buying the same fund in an IRA inside the window can still trigger a wash sale.

lines.text: Next, required minimum distributions, or RMDs. Retirees 73 and older generally have to withdraw a minimum from most retirement accounts.
lines.say: Next, required minimum distributions, or R M Ds. Retirees seventy-three and older generally have to withdraw a minimum from most retirement accounts.

lines.text: The annual deadline is December 31. Only the very first one can wait until April 1 of the next year.
lines.say: The annual deadline is December thirty-first. Only the very first one can wait until April first of the next year.

lines.text: Waiting means two withdrawals in one year. Missing one triggers a 25% excise tax, cut to 10% if fixed in time.
lines.say: Waiting means two withdrawals in one year. Missing one triggers a twenty-five percent excise tax, cut to ten percent if it's fixed in time.

lines.text: Gifts follow the calendar too. For 2026, anyone can give up to $19,000 per person without filing a gift tax return.
lines.say: Gifts follow the calendar too. For twenty twenty-six, anyone can give up to nineteen thousand dollars per person without filing a gift tax return.

lines.text: Each spouse gets their own exclusion, so a married couple can give $38,000 per person. And the limit resets every January 1.
lines.say: Each spouse gets their own exclusion, so a married couple can give thirty-eight thousand dollars per person. And the limit resets every January first.

lines.text: Chapter 5: What the 2025 tax law changed.
lines.say: Chapter five: what the twenty twenty-five tax law changed.

lines.text: The 2025 tax law, often called the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, shifted a few year-end numbers for 2026.
lines.say: The twenty twenty-five tax law, often called the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, shifted a few year-end numbers for twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: The 2026 standard deduction is $16,100 for single filers and $32,200 for married couples filing jointly.
lines.say: The twenty twenty-six standard deduction is sixteen thousand one hundred dollars for single filers, and thirty-two thousand two hundred for married couples filing jointly.

lines.text: The big new one is charity. Starting in 2026, people who take the standard deduction can still deduct cash gifts to qualifying charities.
lines.say: The big new one is charity. Starting in twenty twenty-six, people who take the standard deduction can still deduct cash gifts to qualifying charities.

lines.text: The cap is $1,000 for single filers and $2,000 for joint filers.
lines.say: The cap is one thousand dollars for single filers and two thousand dollars for joint filers.

lines.text: Example: a single filer in the 22% bracket gives $1,000 in cash. That's $220 less federal tax.
lines.say: Example: a single filer in the twenty-two percent bracket gives one thousand dollars in cash. That's two hundred twenty dollars less federal tax.

lines.text: The gift has to be made by December 31, 2026 to count for 2026.
lines.say: The gift has to be made by December thirty-first, twenty twenty-six, to count for twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: People who itemize face a new floor. Only giving above 0.5% of income counts. At $200,000 of income, the first $1,000 doesn't.
lines.say: People who itemize face a new floor. Only giving above half a percent of income counts. At two hundred thousand dollars of income, the first thousand doesn't.

lines.text: The SALT cap on state and local taxes is $40,400 for 2026, up from $10,000 before 2025, and it phases down above $505,000 of income.
lines.say: The SALT cap on state and local taxes is forty thousand four hundred dollars for twenty twenty-six, up from ten thousand before twenty twenty-five, and it phases down above five hundred five thousand of income.

lines.text: For people 65 and older, there's a new deduction of up to $6,000 each, from 2025 through 2028, with income limits.
lines.say: For people sixty-five and older, there's a new deduction of up to six thousand dollars each, from twenty twenty-five through twenty twenty-eight, with income limits.

lines.text: And there are Trump Accounts for kids. Contributions opened July 4, 2026, up to $5,000 a year.
lines.say: And there are Trump Accounts for kids. Contributions opened July fourth, twenty twenty-six, up to five thousand dollars a year.

lines.text: US-citizen kids born 2025 through 2028 can get a $1,000 federal deposit, but a parent has to elect it, on IRS Form 4547.
lines.say: US-citizen kids born twenty twenty-five through twenty twenty-eight can get a one thousand dollar federal deposit, but a parent has to elect it, on IRS Form forty-five forty-seven.

lines.text: In October 2026, Treasury said more than 60 million more kids had been auto-enrolled. A parent still has to claim the account.
lines.say: In October twenty twenty-six, Treasury said more than sixty million more kids had been automatically enrolled. A parent still has to claim the account.

lines.text: Chapter 6: Accounts and goals.
lines.say: Chapter six: accounts and goals.

lines.text: Year-end is a natural time to check credit reports. All three bureaus offer free weekly reports at AnnualCreditReport.com.
lines.say: Year-end is a natural time to check credit reports. All three bureaus offer free weekly reports at Annual Credit Report dot com.

lines.text: Checking your own report doesn't hurt your score. People look for accounts they don't recognize and wrong balances.
lines.say: Checking your own report doesn't hurt your score. People look for accounts they don't recognize and wrong balances.

lines.text: Next, beneficiaries. On a 401(k), IRA or life insurance policy, the beneficiary form usually decides who gets the money, not a will.
lines.say: Next, beneficiaries. On a 401(k), IRA or life insurance policy, the beneficiary form usually decides who gets the money, not a will.

lines.text: Marriage, divorce or a new baby in 2026? Those are the classic reasons a form goes out of date.
lines.say: Marriage, divorce or a new baby in twenty twenty-six? Those are the classic reasons a form goes out of date.

lines.text: Then withholding. If 2026 brought a raise or a side gig, the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator shows whether 2027 paychecks need a new W-4.
lines.say: Then withholding. If twenty twenty-six brought a raise or a side gig, the IRS Tax Withholding Estimator shows whether twenty twenty-seven paychecks need a new W-4.

lines.text: Our last two guides covered the W-2 and a first tax return. Here, it's just saving documents as they arrive.
lines.say: Our last two guides covered the W-2 and a first tax return. Here, it's just saving documents as they arrive.

lines.text: Finally, goals. A simple version is three numbers: what was saved in 2026, the total debt, and one target for 2027.
lines.say: Finally, goals. A simple version is three numbers: what was saved in twenty twenty-six, the total debt, and one target for twenty twenty-seven.

lines.text: A target with a number and a date is easier to track than "save more."
lines.say: A target with a number and a date is easier to track than just saving more.

lines.text: Chapter 7: The one-screen checklist.
lines.say: Chapter seven: the one-screen checklist.

lines.text: By December 31, 2026: the FSA balance, spent or planned for.
lines.say: By December thirty-first, twenty twenty-six: the FSA balance, spent or planned for.

lines.text: 401(k) contributions, through payroll.
lines.say: 401(k) contributions, through payroll.

lines.text: Any gain harvesting or loss harvesting, minding the wash-sale window.
lines.say: Any gain harvesting or loss harvesting, minding the wash-sale window.

lines.text: And RMDs, gifts and charity gifts for 2026.
lines.say: And R M Ds, gifts and charity gifts for twenty twenty-six.

lines.text: By April 15, 2027: IRA contributions for 2026, up to $7,500.
lines.say: By April fifteenth, twenty twenty-seven: IRA contributions for twenty twenty-six, up to seventy-five hundred dollars.

lines.text: HSA contributions, up to $4,400 self-only or $8,750 family.
lines.say: HSA contributions, up to forty-four hundred self-only, or eight thousand seven hundred fifty family.

lines.text: And the 2026 return itself.
lines.say: And the twenty twenty-six return itself.

lines.text: Anytime in December: credit reports, beneficiary forms, withholding, and three goal numbers.
lines.say: Anytime in December: credit reports, beneficiary forms, withholding, and three goal numbers.

lines.text: Back to the start: about half of FSA holders forfeited money in 2022, an average of $441.
lines.say: Back to the start: about half of FSA holders forfeited money in twenty twenty-two, an average of four hundred forty-one dollars.

lines.text: Most of this list isn't about earning more. It's about not missing a date.
lines.say: Most of this list isn't about earning more. It's about not missing a date.

lines.text: Two dates, December 31 and April 15. With both on the calendar, the rest is a checklist.
lines.say: Two dates, December thirty-first and April fifteenth. With both on the calendar, the rest is a checklist.

post.title: Half of FSA holders forfeited money in 2022. Your end-of-year money checklist for 2026.
post.ig: About half of FSA holders forfeited money in 2022. Here's the end-of-year checklist, with every official 2026 limit and deadline.
post.tiktok: Average FSA forfeit in 2022: $441. The two dates that decide your year-end money.
post.yt_desc:
About half of FSA holders forfeited money to their employers in 2022, an average of $441, according to EBRI. This guide walks through the end-of-year money checklist for tax year 2026: what is due by December 31, 2026 versus April 15, 2027; the official 2026 limits for 401(k)s ($24,500, with $8,000 and $11,250 catch-ups and the new Roth catch-up rule), IRAs ($7,500), HSAs ($4,400/$8,750) and FSAs ($3,400, $680 carryover); the 0% capital gains bracket with worked math; tax-loss harvesting and the wash-sale rule; RMDs; the $19,000 gift exclusion; and 2026 changes from the 2025 tax law, including the new $1,000/$2,000 charitable deduction for non-itemizers, the $40,400 SALT cap and Trump Accounts. It ends with credit reports, beneficiaries, withholding, goals and a one-screen checklist.

CHAPTERS

Sources: IRS Notice 2025-67 (Nov 13, 2025); IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-19 (May 1, 2025); IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (Oct 9, 2025); IRS IR-2015-126 and Publication 969; Treasury/IRS final Roth catch-up regulations (Sep 15, 2025); EBRI, Vital Statistics on Flexible Spending Accounts, 2022 (May 2024); Treasury on Trump Accounts auto-enrollment (Oct 1, 2026); FTC on free weekly credit reports; Franklin Templeton and Eaton Vance on 2026 tax law changes (Jan 2026); Morningstar on SECURE 2.0 RMD penalties.

News and education, not financial advice.
